name: Westlake
place: West Lake Hills and surrounding 78746 / 78733, Travis County
schools: Eanes ISD (Westlake High School; confirm campus by address)
setting: Westlake climbs into the hills just west of MoPac and Loop 360, with winding roads, limestone ledges and thick cedar and live oak cover. The City of West Lake Hills is its own small incorporated town, and the western side tends to have the larger, more private lots. It feels secluded but sits minutes from central Austin.
houses: A mix of original 1960s to 1990s ranch and contemporary homes, many being renovated or replaced with new modern and Hill Country custom builds. Wooded lots, often with views, are larger than in central Austin.

todo.name: Wild Basin Wilderness Preserve
todo.line: A 227 acre preserve off Loop 360 with about 2.5 miles of hiking trails.

todo.name: Barton Creek Greenbelt
todo.line: Miles of creekside trail and swimming holes such as Sculpture Falls.

todo.name: Pennybacker Bridge Overlook
todo.line: A short, steep climb to one of the best-known views of the 360 bridge and Lake Austin.

dining.name: Jack Allen's Kitchen (Capital of Texas Hwy)

dining.name: The Grove Wine Bar & Kitchen

dining.name: Taqueria de Diez

clubs.name: Westlake Country Club (formerly Lost Creek Country Club)

name: Tarrytown
schools: Austin ISD (Casis Elementary, O. Henry Middle, Austin High; confirm by address)
setting: Tarrytown is one of central Austin's oldest and most established neighborhoods, set between MoPac and Lake Austin on gently rolling ground. Streets are lined with mature live oaks and pecans, and the lake, Deep Eddy and Lady Bird Lake trails are all close by. It feels residential and quiet while being only a few minutes from downtown.
houses: Original 1930s Tudor and Craftsman cottages and mid-century ranches sit alongside renovations and new contemporary builds. Lots are often around 75 by 150 feet, roughly a quarter acre or more, with big trees.

todo.name: Deep Eddy Pool
todo.line: Spring-fed public pool dating to 1915, open year round.

todo.name: Red Bud Isle
todo.line: A 13 acre island park on Lake Austin, popular as an off-leash dog area.

todo.name: Mayfield Park and Nature Preserve
todo.line: About 23 acres of gardens and trails, known for its resident peacocks.

dining.name: Jeffrey's
dining.line: Long-running Clarksville fine dining spot with a refined American menu.

dining.name: Quince Lakehouse
dining.line: Lake Austin Boulevard restaurant with a global menu and water views.

dining.name: Pool Burger
dining.line: Casual burger and cocktail stand beside Deep Eddy Pool.

clubs.name: Lions Municipal Golf Course
clubs.line: Public 18 hole course open since 1928, right in the neighborhood.

name: Rollingwood
schools: Mostly Eanes ISD (Eanes or Cedar Creek Elementary, Hill Country Middle, Westlake High); a small section may be Austin ISD, so confirm by address
setting: Rollingwood is a small incorporated city of about 1,600 residents with its own police and zoning, tucked between Zilker Park and Bee Caves Road. The ground is flatter than neighboring West Lake Hills, and the streets feel quiet and leafy. Zilker, Barton Springs and the greenbelt are all within a few minutes.
houses: Older ranch homes on generous lots are steadily being replaced by large custom and modern builds. Lots are commonly a quarter acre or more, some approaching a half acre, with mature trees.

todo.name: Zilker Park and Barton Springs Pool
todo.line: Austin's signature 351 acre park and spring-fed pool, just east of town.

todo.name: Barton Creek Greenbelt (Gus Fruh access)
todo.line: Trailhead on the southern edge of the neighborhood.

todo.name: Rollingwood Park
todo.line: Community park on Nixon Drive with a playground and garden.

dining.name: Uchi
dining.line: Acclaimed Japanese restaurant on South Lamar.

dining.name: Odd Duck

dining.name: Chuy's (original)

name: Barton Creek
schools: Split between Eanes ISD and Austin ISD depending on the section (sources disagree; confirm by address)
setting: Barton Creek is a large golf and resort community on rugged Hill Country terrain southwest of downtown, cut by canyons and the creek it is named for. Several gated enclaves sit within it, each with its own character and HOA. Many homes look out over fairways, ravines or long hill views.
houses: Large custom estates in Mediterranean, Texas Hill Country and contemporary styles, plus smaller garden homes in some sections. Lots range from about a quarter acre to three acres or more.

todo.name: Omni Barton Creek Resort and Spa
todo.line: Full resort in the community with spa, pools and dining.

todo.name: Barton Creek Greenbelt
todo.line: Creekside trails and swimming holes reachable from the area.

dining.name: Hill Country Dining Room (Omni Barton Creek)
dining.line: The resort's fine dining room, a long-time AAA Four Diamond holder.

dining.name: Veranda (Omni Barton Creek)
dining.line: Casual resort dining overlooking the Fazio Foothills course.

clubs.name: Barton Creek Country Club / Omni Barton Creek
clubs.line: Four courses: Fazio Foothills, Fazio Canyons, Crenshaw Cliffside and Palmer Lakeside.

clubs.name: Westlake Country Club (formerly Lost Creek Country Club)
clubs.line: Private club just north in Lost Creek.

name: Lake Austin
place: Lake Austin shoreline, Austin and unincorporated Travis County
schools: Varies by shore: Austin ISD, Eanes ISD, Leander ISD or Lake Travis ISD (confirm by address)
setting: Lake Austin is a roughly 20 mile stretch of the Colorado River held at a near-constant level, which makes it ideal for private docks and water sports. The shoreline mixes steep limestone bluffs, quiet coves and wooded hills. Homes run from the eastern shore near Tarrytown out to River Place and Steiner Ranch on the west.
houses: Waterfront estates with private boat docks and lifts are the defining product, alongside some lake-access condos and townhomes. Styles range from classic Texas stone to sharp modern glass designs, and lot sizes vary widely with the shoreline.

todo.name: Mount Bonnell (Covert Park)
todo.line: Classic lookout over Lake Austin reached by a short stair climb.

todo.name: Emma Long Metropolitan Park
todo.line: City park on the lake with swimming, boat ramp and Turkey Creek Trail.

todo.name: Lake Austin Spa Resort
todo.line: Destination spa resort on the water along the western shore.

dining.name: Hula Hut
dining.line: Lakeside Tex-Mex with a big deck over the water on Lake Austin Boulevard.

dining.name: Ski Shores Cafe
dining.line: Laid-back waterfront cafe on Pearce Road, reachable by boat or car.

dining.name: County Line on the Lake
dining.line: Barbecue on Bull Creek just off the lake.

clubs.name: Barton Creek Country Club
clubs.line: Private four course club to the south.

clubs.name: Westlake Country Club (formerly Lost Creek Country Club)
clubs.line: Private club near the central shore.

commute.time: 10 to 30 min, depending on the shore

name: Lakeway and Lake Travis
schools: Lake Travis ISD (Lake Travis High School; confirm campus by address)
setting: Lakeway sits on the south shore of Lake Travis, wedged between the water and rolling Hill Country ridges. Golf courses, marinas and greenbelts are woven through the city, and many streets have lake or canyon views. It is a full-time resort-style town with its own shopping and medical services.
houses: Everything from lock-and-leave condos and golf villas to large waterfront estates, with many homes built from the 1970s on and newer custom builds in gated sections. Lot sizes vary from compact golf course lots to an acre or more on the water.

todo.name: Lakeway City Park
todo.line: A 64 acre park with a paved loop and lake swimming access.

todo.name: Mansfield Dam Park
todo.line: Lakeside county park known for swimming and scuba access.

todo.name: Pace Bend Park
todo.line: Large Travis County park with cliffs and coves about 20 minutes west.

dining.name: The Oasis on Lake Travis
dining.line: Tiered decks with famous sunset views over the lake.

dining.name: Sixty-Three Restaurant and Bar

name: Dripping Springs
place: City of Dripping Springs (78620), Hays County
setting: Dripping Springs sits on US 290 at the edge of the Hill Country, about 25 miles west of downtown Austin, and calls itself a wedding capital thanks to its many ranch venues. The land opens up into rolling pasture, oak motts and creek valleys, with wineries, distilleries and breweries along the back roads. It keeps a small town feel even as new communities grow around it.
houses: Acreage ranches and custom Hill Country homes in stone and metal roofs, along with newer master-planned neighborhoods. Lots range from suburban sites to multi-acre tracts outside town. No reliable recent area-wide price figure found.

todo.name: Hamilton Pool Preserve
todo.line: Collapsed grotto and waterfall; reservations are required, and swimming depends on conditions.

todo.name: Treaty Oak Distilling
todo.line: Distillery on a 24 acre ranch with tastings, tours and live music.

dining.name: The Bistro at Texas Hill Country Olive Co.
dining.line: Daily lunch among olive orchards on West Fitzhugh Road.

dining.name: The Salt Lick BBQ (Driftwood)

name: Georgetown
schools: Georgetown ISD for most of the city (confirm by address)
setting: Georgetown sits about 30 miles north of downtown Austin along I-35, where the San Gabriel River runs through town. Its historic courthouse square is lined with restored Victorian storefronts, and the west side rolls into Hill Country terrain. It mixes small town character with fast-growing new neighborhoods.
houses: Historic homes near the square, golf course neighborhoods, and gated Hill Country enclaves with Tuscan, Mediterranean and stone ranch styles. Luxury lots run from about a quarter acre in golf communities to larger canyon-edge homesites.

todo.name: Georgetown Square
todo.line: Historic courthouse square with shops, restaurants and seasonal festivals.

todo.name: Blue Hole Park
todo.line: Popular swimming spot on the San Gabriel River near downtown.

todo.name: Garey Park
todo.line: A 525 acre park on the west side with trails, fishing and horseback riding.

dining.name: Wildfire

dining.name: Monument Cafe
dining.line: Retro diner with a garden-to-table menu.

dining.name: Goodfolks

name: Spanish Oaks
place: Bee Cave area off Highway 71 (Austin 78738 address), Travis County
schools: Lake Travis ISD (Lake Travis High School; confirm campus by address)
setting: Spanish Oaks is a gated golf community of roughly 900 acres in the hills along Highway 71 near Bee Cave. Large stretches of the land are left as preserved Hill Country, with canyons, elevation changes and long views. Two staffed gatehouses and a private club give it a quiet, secluded feel.
houses: Mostly large custom homes, often 3,500 to 7,000 square feet or more, on homesites from about one acre to five acres or more. Styles lean toward refined Hill Country, Mediterranean and modern.

todo.name: Hamilton Pool Preserve
todo.line: Grotto and waterfall preserve to the west; reservations required.

todo.name: Hill Country Galleria
todo.line: Open-air shopping and dining center in Bee Cave.

clubs.name: Spanish Oaks Golf Club

name: Rough Hollow
schools: Lake Travis ISD (Rough Hollow Elementary, Lake Travis Middle and High are common; confirm by address)
setting: Rough Hollow is a master-planned community on the western edge of Lakeway with about three miles of Lake Travis shoreline. Its signature is a private yacht club and marina, tied to the neighborhoods by a long network of hike and bike trails. Hill Country ridges and canyons frame the newer sections, some of which are still being built.
houses: A wide range, from move-up family homes and lock-and-leave product to custom lakeview and waterfront estates. Styles mix modern farmhouse, Hill Country stone and contemporary designs, on lots that grow larger toward the lake and premium ridges.

todo.name: Rough Hollow Yacht Club and Marina
todo.line: Private marina with slips, pool, fitness center and lake access.

todo.name: Rough Hollow trail network

name: The Hills
place: Village of The Hills, next to Lakeway (78738), Travis County
schools: Lake Travis ISD (confirm campus by address)
setting: The Hills is a gated golf community, set up as its own small village beside Lakeway, built around the courses of The Hills Country Club. Streets wind through hilly, wooded terrain with fairway, canyon and lake views. The Flintrock Falls section adds newer homes on the ridges.
houses: Golf course villas and custom estates, many with stone and stucco exteriors and Hill Country or Mediterranean lines. Lots run from roughly a quarter acre to about two acres.

name: Costa Bella
place: Lake Travis, off RM 620 at Oak Grove Blvd (78734), Travis County

setting: Costa Bella is a small gated enclave of about 62 custom homes on the hills above Lake Travis, between RM 620 and the water. Many homes have sweeping lake views, and residents share a private yacht club. It is quieter and more intimate than the big master-planned communities nearby.
houses: Mostly Mediterranean-style estates in stone and stucco, typically 5,500 to 8,000 plus square feet, built largely in the late 1990s and 2000s. Homesites generally run from one to four acres. No recent dated price data found.

name: Caliterra
setting: Caliterra is a master-planned Hill Country community on the Dripping Springs side of the region, with Onion Creek running through it. Roughly 40 percent of the land is kept as open space, laced with several miles of trails, and the area carries a dark-sky designation that keeps nights starry. Amenities include pools, a fitness center, an on-site restaurant and coffee shop, and campsites.
houses: Custom and semi-custom homes by builders such as Drees and David Weekley, roughly 2,500 to 6,000 square feet, in stone-and-stucco Hill Country and modern farmhouse styles. Homesites are 70, 80 and 110 foot wide lots, with some near an acre.
